head: working-tree
subject: gRPC xDS client status discovery (CSDS)
change: grpc.xds.csds encodes envoy.service.status.v3.ClientStatusResponse without generated protobuf code, and Controller.encodeClientStatus gathers this client's accepted LDS/RDS/CDS/EDS/SDS resources with type URL, name, accepted version, raw wire bytes and status. SotW reports the type's accepted version; delta reports the per-resource accepted version. Subscribed but undelivered resources are included without wire bytes as REQUESTED or DOES_NOT_EXIST, so a dump taken right after start shows what the client is waiting for. Controller.fetchClientStatus validates and decodes one FetchClientStatus request body, ignores node matchers and honors exclude_resource_contents by omitting wire bytes while keeping metadata. grpc.xds.csds_service.respondFetch answers an already-read unary request on the FetchClientStatus path and returns false for other paths, so the application's own admin dispatcher keeps ownership of routing. netz does not own an admin listener.

tests.unit: src/grpc/xds/csds.zig covers response encoding for an accepted resource with wire bytes and a does-not-exist resource without wire. src/grpc/xds/csds_tests.zig drives a delta controller through LDS, RDS, CDS and EDS and checks all four accepted entries with their per-resource version and ACKED status, then drives a SotW controller and checks the accepted listener version plus the pending CDS subscription reported as REQUESTED without a version, exclude_resource_contents dropping wire bytes, ignored node matchers and malformed request rejection. src/grpc/xds/csds_service_tests.zig runs a real h2c server connection, routes the unary request through respondFetch and checks the OK response carries the accepted LDS type URL and name.

interop.result: two emitted responses decoded with the official Envoy csds.proto schema: one client config, node id node-1, scope grpc, three resources with exact type/name/version/status and accepted Any bytes; the exclude_resource_contents response keeps the same metadata with no xds_config

notes: The request's node matchers are ignored because the response describes the local client. Resource status maps requested to REQUESTED, does_not_exist to DOES_NOT_EXIST, a transient timeout to REQUESTED, and a delivered resource to ACKED. The encoder emits proto3 defaults by omission and encodes each accepted resource as a google.protobuf.Any with the resource type URL. The interop gate decodes both responses with protobufjs against the official Envoy proto shipped in the pinned grpc-js-xds dependency. fetchClientStatus bounds the request at 1 MiB and rejects malformed wire types; it ignores node matchers because the response describes the local client. csds_service.respondFetch consumes only requests already routed to FetchClientStatus; the application's dispatcher keeps ownership of every other path.
